Use Case Name: Anonymous Access to Kubernetes API Server
MITRE Tactics: Initial Access; Persistence; Privilege Escalation; Stealth
MITRE Techniques: T1133 External Remote Services; T1078.001 Valid Accounts: Default Accounts
Description: A request was authorised for the user system:anonymous or the group system:unauthenticated on a resource other than health endpoints. Anonymous auth combined with a permissive binding exposes the whole cluster to the internet.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit user.username IN ("system:anonymous") OR "system:unauthenticated" IN user.groups | where responseStatus.code < 400 AND requestURI NOT IN ("/healthz","/livez","/readyz","/version")
False Positives: Load balancer health checks against /healthz, /livez or /readyz.

Use Case Name: Ingress Controller Admission Webhook Exploitation (IngressNightmare)
Log Sources: Falco (Runtime Security); CNI Flow Logs (Cilium Hubble / Calico); Ingress-NGINX Controller Logs
MITRE Techniques: T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application; T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
Description: Detects exploitation of the ingress-nginx admission webhook (CVE-2025-1974 family): AdmissionReview requests reaching the controller from a source other than the API server, followed by nginx loading a shared object from /proc or /tmp, or spawning a shell.
Detection Logic: (flow.dst_pod LIKE "ingress-nginx-controller-*" AND flow.dst_port=8443 AND flow.src_identity != "kube-apiserver") OR (container.image LIKE "*ingress-nginx/controller*" AND (evt.type=openat AND fd.name LIKE "/proc/*/fd/*" AND fd.name ENDS_WITH ".so") OR proc.name IN (sh,bash))
False Positives: Rare. Controller upgrades can briefly produce unusual nginx -t invocations, but never from non-API-server sources.

Use Case Name: Cluster-Admin ClusterRoleBinding Created
MITRE Tactics: Initial Access; Persistence; Privilege Escalation; Stealth
MITRE Techniques: T1098.006 Account Manipulation: Additional Container Cluster Roles; T1078 Valid Accounts
Description: A ClusterRoleBinding or RoleBinding granting cluster-admin (or another highly privileged ClusterRole) was created or patched. Attackers bind their user or a service account to cluster-admin to gain full control and persistence.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.resource IN ("clusterrolebindings","rolebindings") verb IN ("create","update","patch") requestObject.roleRef.name IN ("cluster-admin","admin","system:controller:*") responseStatus.code < 400 | where user.username NOT IN (gitops_service_accounts)
False Positives: Cluster bootstrap, GitOps controllers (Argo CD / Flux) applying approved manifests, break-glass procedures.

Use Case Name: Wildcard RBAC Role or ClusterRole Created
MITRE Techniques: T1098.006 Account Manipulation: Additional Container Cluster Roles
Description: A Role/ClusterRole was created or modified with wildcard verbs or resources, or with escalation verbs (escalate, bind, impersonate) — an effective admin role that bypasses review of cluster-admin bindings.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.resource IN ("roles","clusterroles") verb IN ("create","update","patch") | where requestObject.rules{}.verbs{}="*" OR requestObject.rules{}.resources{}="*" OR requestObject.rules{}.verbs{} IN ("escalate","bind","impersonate")
False Positives: Operator / Helm chart installs (e.g. cert-manager, Prometheus operator) that ship broad roles.

Use Case Name: User Impersonation via Impersonate Headers
MITRE Tactics: Initial Access; Persistence; Privilege Escalation; Stealth
MITRE Techniques: T1078 Valid Accounts
Description: A request carried Impersonate-User / Impersonate-Group headers (audit field impersonatedUser), especially impersonating system:masters, a node identity or a privileged service account. Impersonation lets an identity act with someone else's permissions.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit impersonatedUser.username=* | where impersonatedUser.groups{} IN ("system:masters") OR impersonatedUser.username LIKE "system:node:*" OR impersonatedUser.username LIKE "system:serviceaccount:kube-system:*"
False Positives: Platform admins legitimately using kubectl --as for troubleshooting; some dashboards/proxies (e.g. Rancher, Teleport) impersonate by design.

Use Case Name: Secrets Enumeration Across Namespaces
MITRE Techniques: T1552.007 Unsecured Credentials: Container API; T1613 Container and Resource Discovery
Description: A user or service account listed/watched secrets cluster-wide, or read secrets in many namespaces within a short window. Typical of credential harvesting after initial access.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.resource="secrets" verb IN ("list","watch","get") responseStatus.code=200 | stats dc(objectRef.namespace) AS ns_count, count AS reads BY user.username span=10m | where (ns_count >= 3 OR requestURI="/api/v1/secrets") AND user.username NOT IN (secret_controllers)
False Positives: External Secrets Operator, Vault agent injectors, backup tools (Velero) and Argo CD.

Use Case Name: Service Account Token Used from Outside the Cluster
Log Sources: Kubernetes Audit Log; Cloud Audit Logs (CloudTrail / Azure Activity / GCP Audit)
MITRE Techniques: T1528 Steal Application Access Token; T1550.001 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token
Description: A request authenticated as a service account (system:serviceaccount:*) originated from an IP outside the pod/node CIDRs. Service account tokens should only be used from inside the cluster; external use indicates a stolen token.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit user.username LIKE "system:serviceaccount:*" | where NOT cidrmatch("10.244.0.0/16", sourceIPs{0}) AND NOT cidrmatch("10.0.0.0/16", sourceIPs{0}) | stats values(verb), values(objectRef.resource) BY user.username, sourceIPs{0}, userAgent
False Positives: CI/CD systems outside the cluster that intentionally use a long-lived service account token (should migrate to OIDC).

Use Case Name: CertificateSigningRequest Approved for Privileged Group
MITRE Techniques: T1649 Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
Description: A CSR requesting a client certificate with O=system:masters or a system:node identity was created and approved by a non-controller identity. A signed client cert is a long-lived credential that survives token rotation and cannot be revoked easily.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.resource="certificatesigningrequests" objectRef.subresource="approval" verb IN ("update","patch") | where user.username NOT LIKE "system:kube-controller-manager" | join objectRef.name [search verb=create objectRef.resource=certificatesigningrequests requestObject.spec.signerName="kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client"]
False Positives: Manual onboarding of administrators via CSR workflow (should be rare and ticketed).

Use Case Name: Permission Probing – Burst of Forbidden (403) Responses
MITRE Techniques: T1069 Permission Groups Discovery; T1613 Container and Resource Discovery
Description: A single identity receives many 403 Forbidden responses across different resources in a short time, or issues SelfSubjectAccessReview / SelfSubjectRulesReview requests (kubectl auth can-i --list) — typical of tools such as kube-hunter, peirates or manual post-exploitation recon.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit (responseStatus.code=403 OR objectRef.resource IN ("selfsubjectrulesreviews","selfsubjectaccessreviews")) | stats count, dc(objectRef.resource) AS res BY user.username, sourceIPs{0} span=5m | where count > 20 AND res > 5
False Positives: Misconfigured controllers after an RBAC change; developers exploring access with kubectl auth can-i.

Use Case Name: kubectl exec / attach / debug into Pod
MITRE Techniques: T1609 Container Administration Command
Description: Interactive command execution inside a running pod via pods/exec, pods/attach or an ephemeral debug container (pods/ephemeralcontainers). Legitimate for operators but a primary hands-on-keyboard technique for attackers, especially in production namespaces.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.subresource IN ("exec","attach","ephemeralcontainers") verb IN ("create","get","patch","update") responseStatus.code=101 OR responseStatus.code=200 | where objectRef.namespace IN (prod_namespaces) | stats count BY user.username, objectRef.namespace, objectRef.name, requestURI
False Positives: On-call engineers troubleshooting, liveness tooling and some CI pipelines. Tune per namespace and user group.

Use Case Name: Exec into kube-system or Control-Plane Pod
MITRE Techniques: T1609 Container Administration Command; T1611 Escape to Host
Description: pods/exec or pods/attach targeting pods in kube-system (CoreDNS, kube-proxy, CNI agents, etcd, static control-plane pods). These pods often run privileged with host access or powerful service account tokens.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.subresource IN ("exec","attach") objectRef.namespace IN ("kube-system","kube-public","calico-system","cilium") | where user.username NOT IN (break_glass_admins)
False Positives: Platform team debugging CNI/DNS issues during a declared incident.

Use Case Name: Direct etcd Access from Unauthorized Client
Log Sources: etcd Logs; CNI Flow Logs (Cilium Hubble / Calico); Host Firewall / VPC Flow Logs
MITRE Techniques: T1552.007 Unsecured Credentials: Container API; T1613 Container and Resource Discovery
Description: Connections to etcd client port 2379 (or peer port 2380) from any host other than the API servers / etcd peers, or TLS handshake rejections at etcd. etcd stores every Secret — direct access bypasses RBAC and audit logging entirely.
Detection Logic: (source=flow dst_port IN (2379,2380) NOT src_ip IN (apiserver_ips, etcd_peer_ips)) OR (source=etcd msg IN ("rejected connection on client endpoint","rejected connection on peer endpoint"))
False Positives: etcd backup jobs and monitoring scrapers (add their IPs to the allow-list).

Use Case Name: Port-Forward or API Proxy Tunnel to Internal Service
MITRE Techniques: T1572 Protocol Tunneling
Description: Use of pods/portforward, services/proxy or nodes/proxy subresources to tunnel traffic through the API server into internal services (databases, admin UIs, kubelet) that are not exposed externally.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.subresource IN ("portforward","proxy") | where objectRef.resource="nodes" OR objectRef.namespace IN (prod_namespaces) | stats count BY user.username, objectRef.resource, objectRef.namespace, objectRef.name
False Positives: Developers port-forwarding to dev databases; metrics-server and dashboards using services/proxy.

Use Case Name: Kubernetes Events Deleted
MITRE Techniques: T1070 Indicator Removal
Description: Deletion of Event objects (core/v1 events or events.k8s.io) by a human or non-controller identity. Events reveal pod scheduling, image pulls and failures; deleting them hides attacker activity from operators.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.resource="events" verb IN ("delete","deletecollection") | where user.username NOT LIKE "system:*"
False Positives: Very rare; events expire automatically via TTL so manual deletion is unusual.

Use Case Name: Mass Deletion of Workloads or Namespaces
MITRE Techniques: T1485 Data Destruction; T1489 Service Stop
Description: A single identity deletes namespaces, deployments, statefulsets, PVCs or PVs in volume within minutes — destructive impact or ransomware-style extortion against a cluster.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit verb IN ("delete","deletecollection") objectRef.resource IN ("namespaces","deployments","statefulsets","persistentvolumeclaims","persistentvolumes") responseStatus.code < 400 | stats count, dc(objectRef.namespace) BY user.username span=10m | where count >= 10 OR objectRef.resource="namespaces"
False Positives: Ephemeral preview environments torn down by CI; planned decommissioning.

Use Case Name: Privileged Pod Created
Log Sources: Kubernetes Audit Log; Admission Controller (Kyverno / OPA Gatekeeper / PSA)
MITRE Techniques: T1610 Deploy Container; T1611 Escape to Host
Description: A pod (or workload template) was created with securityContext.privileged=true or allowPrivilegeEscalation=true outside approved system namespaces. Privileged containers have full access to host devices and are one step from host compromise.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.resource="pods" verb="create" | spath requestObject.spec.containers{}.securityContext.privileged AS priv | where priv="true" AND objectRef.namespace NOT IN ("kube-system","calico-system","falco")
False Positives: CNI, CSI and security agents (Falco, Cilium, node-exporter) that legitimately run privileged.

Use Case Name: Sensitive hostPath Volume Mounted
Log Sources: Kubernetes Audit Log; Admission Controller (Kyverno / OPA Gatekeeper / PSA)
MITRE Techniques: T1611 Escape to Host; T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
Description: A pod mounts a sensitive host directory: /, /etc, /root, /proc, /var/lib/kubelet, /etc/kubernetes, /var/run/docker.sock or /run/containerd/containerd.sock. This gives direct read/write access to node credentials and the container runtime.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.resource="pods" verb="create" | spath requestObject.spec.volumes{}.hostPath.path AS hp | where hp IN ("/","/etc","/root","/proc","/var/lib/kubelet","/etc/kubernetes","/var/run/docker.sock","/run/containerd/containerd.sock")
False Positives: Log shippers (Fluent Bit mounting /var/log), node-exporter (/proc, /sys), CSI drivers.

Use Case Name: Pod Using Host Namespaces (hostPID / hostNetwork / hostIPC)
Log Sources: Kubernetes Audit Log; Admission Controller (Kyverno / OPA Gatekeeper / PSA)
MITRE Techniques: T1611 Escape to Host; T1613 Container and Resource Discovery
Description: A pod requests hostPID, hostNetwork or hostIPC. hostPID allows nsenter into PID 1 and reading other processes' environments; hostNetwork exposes node interfaces and bypasses NetworkPolicy.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.resource="pods" verb="create" (requestObject.spec.hostPID=true OR requestObject.spec.hostNetwork=true OR requestObject.spec.hostIPC=true) | where objectRef.namespace NOT IN (system_namespaces)
False Positives: kube-proxy, CNI daemonsets, node monitoring agents, ingress controllers using hostNetwork.

Use Case Name: Dangerous Linux Capabilities Added to Container
Log Sources: Kubernetes Audit Log; Admission Controller (Kyverno / OPA Gatekeeper / PSA)
MITRE Techniques: T1611 Escape to Host; T1068 Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
Description: Container securityContext.capabilities.add contains SYS_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, SYS_MODULE, DAC_READ_SEARCH, NET_ADMIN, NET_RAW or BPF. These capabilities enable known container escape techniques (cgroup release_agent, ptrace injection, kernel module loading).
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.resource="pods" verb="create" | spath requestObject.spec.containers{}.securityContext.capabilities.add{} AS caps | where caps IN ("SYS_ADMIN","SYS_PTRACE","SYS_MODULE","DAC_READ_SEARCH","NET_ADMIN","BPF","ALL")
False Positives: eBPF-based observability/security tools (Cilium, Falco, Pixie), VPN sidecars needing NET_ADMIN.

Use Case Name: Workload Deployed to kube-system by Non-System Identity
MITRE Techniques: T1036.005 Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location; T1610 Deploy Container
Description: Pods, Deployments or DaemonSets created in kube-system by a human user or a non-system service account, often with names mimicking legitimate components (kube-proxy-x, coredns-helper). Attackers hide in kube-system because it is rarely reviewed.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.namespace="kube-system" verb="create" objectRef.resource IN ("pods","deployments","daemonsets","replicasets","jobs") | where user.username NOT LIKE "system:*" AND user.username NOT IN (platform_gitops_sa)
False Positives: Platform engineers installing add-ons via Helm directly (should go through GitOps).

Use Case Name: Suspicious CronJob Created
MITRE Techniques: T1053.007 Scheduled Task/Job: Container Orchestration Job
Description: A CronJob is created or modified with a high-frequency schedule, an image from an unapproved registry, a shell/curl/wget command, or in a system namespace. CronJobs provide stealthy recurring execution and persistence.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.resource="cronjobs" verb IN ("create","update","patch") | spath requestObject.spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers{}.command{} AS cmd | where match(cmd, "(curl|wget|sh -c|bash -c|base64|nc )") OR objectRef.namespace="kube-system" OR requestObject.spec.schedule="* * * * *"
False Positives: Backup, report and cleanup CronJobs using shell wrappers; tune by image allow-list.

Use Case Name: DaemonSet Created or Modified (Cluster-Wide Persistence)
MITRE Techniques: T1543.005 Create or Modify System Process: Container Service; T1610 Deploy Container
Description: A new DaemonSet, or an image/command change to an existing one, outside the GitOps pipeline. DaemonSets run on every node (including new ones), giving attackers instant cluster-wide persistence — commonly used to deploy miners.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.resource="daemonsets" verb IN ("create","update","patch") responseStatus.code < 400 | where user.username NOT IN (gitops_service_accounts) | table requestReceivedTimestamp, user.username, objectRef.namespace, objectRef.name, requestObject.spec.template.spec.containers{}.image
False Positives: Add-on installs/upgrades (logging, monitoring, CNI) performed manually.

Use Case Name: Admission Webhook or Policy Engine Deleted / Weakened
MITRE Techniques: T1685 Disable or Modify Tools
Description: Deletion or modification of ValidatingWebhookConfiguration / MutatingWebhookConfiguration objects, Kyverno/Gatekeeper policies, failurePolicy changed to Ignore, or the Pod Security Admission label on a namespace lowered to privileged.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit ((objectRef.resource IN ("validatingwebhookconfigurations","mutatingwebhookconfigurations","clusterpolicies","constrainttemplates") verb IN ("delete","update","patch")) OR (objectRef.resource="namespaces" verb IN ("update","patch") requestObject.metadata.labels."pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce"="privileged")) | where user.username NOT IN (policy_operator_sa)
False Positives: Policy engine upgrades; cert rotation rewriting caBundle on webhooks (filter caBundle-only patches).

Use Case Name: NetworkPolicy Deleted or Default-Deny Removed
MITRE Techniques: T1686.001 Disable or Modify System Firewall: Cloud Firewall
Description: NetworkPolicy, CiliumNetworkPolicy or Calico GlobalNetworkPolicy objects deleted or modified to allow all ingress/egress — removes segmentation to enable lateral movement or exfiltration.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.resource IN ("networkpolicies","ciliumnetworkpolicies","globalnetworkpolicies") verb IN ("delete","deletecollection","patch","update") | where user.username NOT IN (gitops_service_accounts)
False Positives: Application teams iterating on policies in non-production namespaces.

Use Case Name: Control-Plane Audit Logging Disabled (EKS / AKS / GKE)
Log Sources: Cloud Audit Logs (CloudTrail / Azure Activity / GCP Audit)
MITRE Techniques: T1685.002 Disable or Modify Tools: Disable or Modify Cloud Log
Description: Managed Kubernetes control-plane logging (api, audit, authenticator) was disabled: EKS UpdateClusterConfig with enabled=false, AKS diagnostic setting deleted, or GKE logging component removed. Blinds every audit-based detection in this library.
Detection Logic: (source=aws:cloudtrail eventSource="eks.amazonaws.com" eventName="UpdateClusterConfig" requestParameters.logging.clusterLogging{}.enabled=false) OR (source=azure:activity operationName="MICROSOFT.INSIGHTS/DIAGNOSTICSETTINGS/DELETE" resourceId="*managedClusters*") OR (source=gcp:audit methodName="google.container.v1.ClusterManager.UpdateCluster" request.update.desiredLoggingConfig=*)
False Positives: Cost-reduction changes in sandbox accounts (should be change-managed).

Use Case Name: Image from Untrusted or Public Registry Deployed
MITRE Techniques: T1204.003 User Execution: Malicious Image; T1525 Implant Internal Image
Description: A workload references an image outside the approved registry allow-list (e.g. docker.io personal namespaces, ghcr.io unknown orgs, raw IPs), or uses a mutable :latest tag without a digest in production.
Detection Logic: source=k8s_audit objectRef.resource IN ("pods","deployments","daemonsets","statefulsets","cronjobs","jobs") verb IN ("create","patch","update") | spath output=img path=requestObject..image | where NOT match(img, "^(123456789012\.dkr\.ecr\..*|registry\.corp\.example/|registry\.k8s\.io/)")
False Positives: Developers testing public images in sandbox namespaces; vendor images from new registries.

Use Case Name: Image Signature or Admission Policy Verification Failure
Log Sources: Admission Controller (Kyverno / OPA Gatekeeper / PSA); Kubernetes Audit Log
MITRE Techniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain; T1525 Implant Internal Image
Description: An admission controller (Kyverno verifyImages, Sigstore policy-controller, Connaisseur, Ratify) rejected or audited an image whose Cosign/Notary signature or attestation is missing or invalid — possibly a tampered image in an internal registry.
Detection Logic: (source=kyverno policyReport.results{}.result="fail" policyReport.results{}.policy="verify-image-signatures") OR (source=k8s_audit responseStatus.code=400 responseStatus.message="*image signature verification failed*")
False Positives: New images pushed before the signing step completed in CI; key rotation.

Use Case Name: Interactive Shell Spawned in Container
MITRE Techniques: T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell; T1609 Container Administration Command
Description: A shell (sh, bash, ash, zsh) with an attached TTY started inside a container, either through kubectl exec or spawned by the application process (e.g. java → sh) indicating remote code execution.
Detection Logic: source=falco rule="Terminal shell in container" OR (evt.type=execve AND container.id!=host AND proc.name IN (sh,bash,ash,zsh) AND proc.pname IN (java,node,python,php-fpm,nginx,httpd))
False Positives: Debugging sessions by operators, init scripts using sh -c (no TTY).

Use Case Name: Container Escape Attempt (nsenter / release_agent / host mount)
MITRE Techniques: T1611 Escape to Host
Description: Behaviour associated with breaking out of a container: nsenter targeting PID 1, writes to cgroup release_agent / notify_on_release, mounting host block devices, chroot to a host mount, or exploiting runc (/proc/self/exe overwrite).
Detection Logic: source=falco rule IN ("Detect release_agent File Container Escapes","Mount Launched in Privileged Container","Change namespace privileges via unshare") OR (container.id!=host AND proc.name="nsenter" AND proc.args LIKE "*-t 1*") OR (evt.type=open AND fd.name ENDS_WITH "release_agent")
False Positives: Node debugging tools (kubectl debug node/…, node-shell) used by administrators.

Use Case Name: Container Drift – New Binary Dropped and Executed
MITRE Techniques: T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer; T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
Description: An executable that was not part of the original image is written to the container filesystem and executed (immutable-container drift), or a package manager (apt, yum, apk, pip) runs in a running container to install tooling.

Use Case Name: Service Account Token or Sensitive File Read by Unexpected Process
MITRE Techniques: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files; T1528 Steal Application Access Token
Description: A shell, cat, curl or other non-application process reads /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token, /etc/shadow, kubeconfig files, or cloud credential files inside a container.
Detection Logic: source=falco rule IN ("Read sensitive file untrusted","Read sensitive file trusted after startup") OR (container.id!=host AND evt.type IN (open,openat) AND fd.name IN ("/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token","/etc/shadow","/root/.kube/config","/root/.aws/credentials") AND proc.name IN (cat,sh,bash,curl,python,base64,head,tail))

Use Case Name: Cloud Instance Metadata (IMDS) Accessed from Pod

MITRE Techniques: T1552.005 Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API
Description: A non-system pod connects to 169.254.169.254 / metadata.google.internal / 169.254.170.2 to retrieve node IAM role credentials — common SSRF and post-exploitation pivot from container to cloud account.

Use Case Name: Reverse Shell from Container
Log Sources: Falco (Runtime Security); EDR / Linux auditd; CNI Flow Logs (Cilium Hubble / Calico)
MITRE Techniques: T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell; T1095 Non-Application Layer Protocol
Description: A shell process has its stdin/stdout redirected to a network socket (bash -i >& /dev/tcp/…, nc -e, socat exec, python pty spawn) — an interactive attacker channel out of the cluster.
Detection Logic: source=falco rule IN ("Redirect STDOUT/STDIN to Network Connection in Container","Netcat Remote Code Execution in Container") OR (evt.type=dup2 AND fd.type IN (ipv4,ipv6) AND proc.name IN (sh,bash,python,perl,socat) AND container.id!=host)

Use Case Name: Network Scanning Tool Executed in Container
Log Sources: Falco (Runtime Security); CNI Flow Logs (Cilium Hubble / Calico)
MITRE Techniques: T1046 Network Service Discovery; T1613 Container and Resource Discovery
Description: nmap, masscan, zmap, kube-hunter or similar tools executed in a container, or a pod contacting a large number of distinct IP:port pairs (east-west scan of services, kubelet 10250, etcd 2379).
Detection Logic: (source=falco evt.type=execve proc.name IN (nmap,masscan,zmap,kube-hunter,peirates,netexec)) OR (source=flow | stats dc(dst_ip) AS hosts, dc(dst_port) AS ports BY src_pod span=1m | where hosts > 50 OR ports > 100)

Use Case Name: Kernel Module Loaded from Container
MITRE Techniques: T1547.006 Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Kernel Modules and Extensions; T1611 Escape to Host
Description: init_module / finit_module syscall, insmod or modprobe executed from inside a container (requires CAP_SYS_MODULE). Loading a kernel module from a container compromises the node kernel — typical of rootkits (e.g. Diamorphine).
Detection Logic: source=falco rule="Linux Kernel Module Injection Detected" OR (evt.type IN (init_module,finit_module) AND container.id!=host) OR (source=auditd syscall IN (init_module,finit_module) AND cgroup LIKE "*kubepods*")

Use Case Name: Container Runtime Socket Accessed from Container
Log Sources: Falco (Runtime Security); Docker Daemon Logs / Events; Kubernetes Audit Log
MITRE Techniques: T1611 Escape to Host; T1610 Deploy Container; T1059.013 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Container CLI/API
Description: A process inside a container connects to /var/run/docker.sock, /run/containerd/containerd.sock or /var/run/crio/crio.sock. Access to the runtime socket allows launching a privileged container on the host, equivalent to node root.
Detection Logic: (source=falco evt.type=connect AND fd.name IN ("/var/run/docker.sock","/run/containerd/containerd.sock","/var/run/crio/crio.sock") AND container.id!=host) OR (source=docker action=create Actor.Attributes.privileged=true initiated_from_container=true)
False Positives: CI runners using Docker-in-Docker, monitoring agents (cAdvisor, Datadog) — prefer rootless builders (Kaniko, BuildKit).

Use Case Name: Exposed Docker Remote API Used to Create or Build Containers
Log Sources: Docker Daemon Logs / Events; Host Firewall / VPC Flow Logs
MITRE Techniques: T1133 External Remote Services; T1610 Deploy Container; T1612 Build Image on Host; T1059.013 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Container CLI/API
Description: The Docker Engine API on TCP 2375/2376 receives container create, exec or image build calls from an external or non-management IP. Unauthenticated Docker APIs are mass-exploited for cryptomining (TeamTNT, Kinsing) and attackers build images directly on the host to evade registry scanning.
Detection Logic: (source=dockerd msg="API listen on *:2375") OR (source=dockerd msg IN ("Calling POST */containers/create","Calling POST */build","Calling POST */exec") remote_addr NOT IN (mgmt_cidrs)) OR (source=flow dst_port IN (2375,2376) direction=inbound src_ip NOT IN (mgmt_cidrs))
False Positives: Legacy build hosts with remote Docker access from CI (should use TLS client certs and allow-lists).

Use Case Name: Static Pod Manifest or Kubelet Config Tampered on Node
Log Sources: EDR / Linux auditd; File Integrity Monitoring; Kubelet Logs
MITRE Techniques: T1543.005 Create or Modify System Process: Container Service; T1685 Disable or Modify Tools
Description: Files created or modified in /etc/kubernetes/manifests (static pods), /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml, kubelet systemd drop-ins, or /etc/containerd/config.toml. Static pods are started by kubelet directly, bypass admission control, and survive API-level clean-up; config changes can enable anonymous auth or disable authorization.
Detection Logic: source=auditd key IN ("k8s_manifests","kubelet_config") syscall IN (openat,rename,unlink) success=yes exe NOT IN ("/usr/bin/kubeadm","/usr/bin/kubelet") OR (source=kubelet msg="*Static pod*" AND file NOT IN (baseline_manifests))
False Positives: kubeadm upgrades, configuration management (Ansible, Chef) runs during maintenance windows.

Use Case Name: Unauthenticated or Anomalous Kubelet API Access (10250)
Log Sources: Kubelet Logs; Host Firewall / VPC Flow Logs; Kubernetes Audit Log
MITRE Techniques: T1609 Container Administration Command; T1133 External Remote Services
Description: Requests to the kubelet API (/run, /exec, /pods, /runningpods, /configz) on 10250/10255 from sources other than the API server or metrics-server, or kubelet authz checks (subjectaccessreviews by system:node) for unexpected users. Detection Logic: (source=kubelet URI IN ("/run/*","/exec/*","/runningpods/*","/pods","/configz") srcIP NOT IN (apiserver_ips, metrics_server_ips)) OR (source=flow dst_port IN (10250,10255) src_ip NOT IN (apiserver_ips, metrics_server_ips, monitoring_cidrs))
False Positives: Prometheus scraping /metrics, metrics-server, kubectl logs/exec proxied via the API server.
